methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

actual_scope: Whether an interleaved word meets the g=31, q=26 paired-star endpoint with five rank-q thin maps when full projectors need not commute. This package fixes one all-first-then-all-second order and one legal noncommuting frame, imposes the thin maps forced by D_j=1, and shows the pure product and the normalized coefficient miss the endpoint.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a changed caller or query demand removes real work, and its first experiment points at the paired-star objections in #5747. The assigned question is the interleaved g=31, q=26 profile left open by PR #7010. The result is one call order and one frame, not a new caller and not a change of kappa.
bottleneck_link: A cheaper paired-star caller would need a complete endpoint at this profile. This order and frame do not supply one: the pure product already misses the target, so the five rank-q maps forced by D_j=1 cannot remove the extra maps.
stop_rule: Fix one separating pattern, impose the D_j=1 thin maps, and test the normalized coefficient at two field points. Do not treat a failed search as unrestricted nonexistence, do not lift the g=3 census, and do not change kappa.
evidence: PROOF.md together with verify.py. The 6-by-6 difference is the exact polynomial product. The two GF(16) points evaluate that identity and the normalized coefficient of the forced rank-q maps.

open_questions.question: Does this same all-first-then-all-second order meet the g=31, q=26 endpoint for some other legal frame whose stage eigenbases are not the same?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The explicit frame in this package fails for every thin map. A different noncommuting frame could still make the pure product match, and the commuting map-count does not cover that frame.
open_questions.first_step: Form the two-stage cross product for one pair of legal frames that are not conjugate to the same (A, B), and compare one off-diagonal block with the target before any native bill.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing external. This package fixes one frame and does not run that second calculation.

open_questions.question: Can a word that separates a stage only by thin maps, with no other full call between the halves, meet the g=31, q=26 endpoint with five rank-26 maps?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That schedule keeps the pure factor product_j (I+x_j E_j), so the pure-product defect proved here does not apply. It is the internal-gap question left by PR #7005.
open_questions.first_step: Read the core-to-leaf coefficient of that internal gap in the eigenbasis of its projector, with the off-diagonal blocks free, as already named by PR #7005.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package's specialization sets the other full calls between the halves. It does not analyze an open stage whose only interior calls are thin.
